title: Sir James Somerville is Lord Mayor of Dublin
desc: James Somerville, MP for Dublin City since 1729, serves as Lord Mayor {s:wp-sir-james-somerville}.

title: Somerville baronetcy created
desc: James Somerville is created a baronet "of Somerville, Co. Meath"; he dies that August and is succeeded by his eldest son Quaile {s:wp-sir-james-somerville}. The narrator's "first baronet" {q:84}.

title: Major William Somerville inherits Ardrass
desc: The second son of the first baronet "inherited an estate in County Kildare called Ardrass … a large house and a lot of land", let to tenants as was usual {q:84-86}. The NLI pedigree of the Somervilles of Ardrass begins in 1752 {s:nli-ardrass}.

title: Henry Bellingham marries Elizabeth Tenison
desc: Eliza Bellingham's parents marry in Dublin {s:lf-bellingham}. The Tenison name will reappear in two generations.

title: Captain William Somerville born
desc: Born on 7 March and baptised at St Thomas', Dublin, on 11 March 1776, according to the family's printed pedigree {s:visitation-1897}; Kingsley also gives 1776 {s:lf-bellingham}, and Stirnet 3 March {s:winters-p67}. The narrator remembered "born in 1777, I think" {q:62} {q:T2:30}; reading the family Bible in the second recording he was heard as saying "born on the 7th of March, 1778" {q:T3:28} ({qn:q-family-bible}).

title: Eliza Bellingham born
desc: The second of three daughters of Colonel Henry Bellingham of Castle Bellingham, born 5 September 1779 {s:visitation-1897} {s:lf-bellingham}. The family Bible, as heard in the second recording, gives "the 8th of September 1772" {q:T3:29}, which cannot be right for a second daughter whose parents married in June 1772 ({qn:q-family-bible}).

title: Alan Bellingham marries Monique Bâby at Detroit
desc: Eliza's brother Alan, who had gone to Canada as a young man, marries the French-Canadian Monique Bâby {q:30} {s:lf-bellingham}.

title: William Bellingham, Pitt's secretary, made a baronet
desc: Created baronet "of Castle Bellingham" with remainder to his father's heirs {s:wp-bellingham-bt}.

title: Rebellion of 1798
desc: The United Irishmen's rising. Irish militia regiments, including the North and South Cork regiments in which Captain William may have served {q:54-56} {q:T2:27-28}, saw heavy service in it {s:wp-irish-militia}.

title: Captain William Somerville marries Eliza Bellingham
desc: "He married Eliza Bellingham, I think 1800" {q:60-62}; the published genealogy gives Roscrea, 30 August 1800 {s:lf-bellingham}. Half his interest in Ardrass goes into the marriage settlement {q:88-90}.

title: Lt-Col. Henry Bellingham dies; Alan inherits Castle Bellingham
desc: Published account {s:lf-bellingham}.

title: Archibald James Somerville born
desc: "He was born in 1803, is it? Yes" {q:128} {q:T2:57}. A compiled genealogy gives 13 May 1803 {s:winters-p67}.

title: Henry Tenison Bellingham killed at Badajoz
desc: Eliza's younger brother, a captain, is killed in the storming of Badajoz {q:44, 52} {s:lf-bellingham}. Years later Eliza writes on the anniversary that her brother "was killed on this day, so many years ago".

title: Siege of Badajoz
desc: Wellington's Anglo-Portuguese army besieges and storms the French-held fortress; the assault costs thousands of allied casualties {s:wp-badajoz}. (Waterloo, which the narrator wondered about, was in 1815; the "War of 1812" was a separate Anglo-American conflict.)

title: Alan and Monique Bellingham separate
desc: "Their marriage was not successful" {q:40}. Monique settles at Lyme Regis, Alan in London {s:lf-bellingham}.

title: Castle Bellingham passes to Sir William Bellingham
desc: Narrator: Alan "sold it, actually, to his uncle" {q:36-38}. Published account: Alan had rented the estate to Sir William, and his widow sold the freehold by about 1824 {s:lf-bellingham}.

title: Archibald James leaves home for Barbados
desc: While "Eliza and I and Dorothea" were in Dublin (so transcript B; A omits "I"), Archibald, aged 19, left home, "spent a few days in Clonmel, and then taken ship on board the George and Thomas for the Barbados". He had "got a girl into the family way" {q:16-18} {q:142-150} {q:T2:8-9} {q:T2:63-65}.

title: Birth of "little Archie"
desc: Letters arrive from Madeira and Barbados; one names the child Archibald. Captain William and Eliza take responsibility for "little Archie", paying a succession of wet nurses {q:154-162} {q:T2:65-68}.

title: Sir William Bellingham dies
desc: Succeeded by his nephew Sir Alan, 2nd Bt, whose line held Castle Bellingham until c. 1956 {s:wp-bellingham-bt}.

title: The family moves from Cumry to "Farm", then to Dublin
desc: From Cumry to a house "just called Farm" (probably near Belturbet, Co. Cavan) for a few years, then to Bayview Avenue/Crescent, Dublin {q:182-184}. Dates not given.

title: Irish Constabulary formed
desc: The Irish Constabulary Act amalgamates the provincial forces into a single armed, centrally controlled Irish Constabulary {s:wp-ric}.

title: Eliza Somerville (née Bellingham) dies
desc: "Eliza died, 1839" {q:186}; "the family then went into decline" {q:198}. She died on 16 December and was buried at St Audoen's on 19 December 1839 {s:visitation-1897} {s:lf-bellingham}. The family Bible, as read aloud in the second recording, has her die "on the 18th of December 1839 at Bayview Avenue in the City of Dublin" {q:T3:29}.

title: Tenison Alan returns from Trinidad
desc: After his mother's death he "returned to Ireland in 1840 … and secured an appointment. They were always looking for appointments, particularly in the West Indies" {q:204} {q:T2:83}.

title: Deaths of Bellingham and of Captain William Somerville
desc: Father and son had moved to lodgings north of the Liffey. "Bellingham died in the autumn of 1844 and Captain William died in December 1844" {q:198-200} {q:T2:81-82}. The family's 1897 pedigree gives the days: Bellingham died on 17 November (buried at St Audoen's on 19 November) and Captain William on 19 December (buried there on 21 December) 1844 {s:visitation-1897}. The compiled genealogy's 1845 for Bellingham is wrong {s:winters-p67}.

title: Captain William and his son Bellingham admitted to the Freedom of Dublin
desc: The 1897 pedigree records the admission of Captain William Somerville and his son Bellingham to the Freedom of the City of Dublin on 10 January 1842; Tenison Alan followed in 1883 and Bellingham Arthur in 1893 {s:visitation-1897}. The narrator, reading the pedigree: "Bellingham also got the freedom of the city of Dublin … You could get the freedom of the city by descent … So it doesn't actually mean very much" {q:T3:17-18}.

title: Tenison Alan copies his father's family record
desc: An envelope in the narrator's keeping holds "one small page of the original family record entered in the family Bible by Captain William Somerville", a "copy of the entire record of Captain William Somerville made by his son T.A. in 1850", and Tenison Alan's own "record of the births of his children made in the family Bible" {q:T3:34}.

title: The Great Famine
desc: Potato blight brings famine, mass death and emigration. The narrator does not mention it, but it frames the years in which Tenison Alan built his career at Dublin Castle and his cousin Sir William served as Chief Secretary {s:wp-great-famine} {s:wp-1st-baron}.

title: Sir William Somerville is Chief Secretary for Ireland
desc: Tenison's "cousin" holds the office that made him, in effect, the minister governing Ireland {s:wp-1st-baron} {s:wp-chief-secretary}; the narrator credits him with Tenison's Constabulary appointment {q:212-214} {q:T2:86-87}.

title: Bellingham Arthur Somerville born
desc: Born 17 November 1853 and baptised in Dublin on 16 June 1854, according to the IGI as quoted in a compiled genealogy {s:winters-p68}; his RIC enlistment age and 1891 census age agree. The narrator remembered "the year of the Crimean War … I think it was 1856" {q:2} {q:T2:1-2}; the war began in 1853.

title: Monique Bellingham dies at Lyme Regis
desc: Published account {s:lf-bellingham}.

title: The Constabulary becomes "Royal"
desc: After the Fenian Rising of 1867 the Irish Constabulary is granted the prefix "Royal" {s:wp-ric}.

title: Archibald James Somerville dies
desc: "He died in 1871, I think" {q:128}. The family's 1897 pedigree confirms it: died 7 February 1871, place not given {s:visitation-1897}.

title: W. A. T. B. ("Bunt") Somerville born
desc: Born at Newtownards, according to the family tree; his ages in 1891 and at his death in 1951 agree {s:family-tree-2026} {s:winters-p69}. The narrator: "born in about 1884" {q:264} {q:T2:103}.

title: The Plan of Campaign
desc: Tenants on selected estates withhold rent collectively during the agricultural depression; the Ponsonby estate near Youghal is among the first targeted {s:wp-plan-of-campaign} {s:ballymacoda-1887}.

title: The Youghal riot: Patrick Hanlon killed
desc: Family account: a riot at Youghal "got out of hand"; RIC were sent by train from Cork "under the command of Captain Somerville"; "some rioter called Hanlon or O'Hanlon" was killed with a sabre; Somerville and the man responsible were "had up", suspended, the matter "went as far as Parliament", and he was reinstated but, in the narrator's words, "never formally acquitted" {q:312-322} {q:T2:118-127}. Local history: Patrick Hanlon, a 30-year-old fisherman from Ballymacoda, was killed on 8 March 1887 by a sword bayonet when the RIC charged a crowd protesting at the arrest of Fr Daniel Keller (a Plan of Campaign case); the coroner's jury found wilful murder against District Inspector Somerville and Constable Garrett Ward, who were held in Cork; the Crown entered a nolle prosequi {s:ballymacoda-1887}. Hansard: the wilful-murder verdict and custody (24 March) {s:hansard-1887}; on 10 May, "Sub-Inspector Summerville" and Ward on bail, on leave with pay, to return to duty, as the Attorney General saw "no grounds to advise a prosecution" {s:hansard-1887c}. {int}The records give only the surname, but the officer is identified as Bellingham Arthur Somerville on the combined evidence: a serving RIC officer of that rank (joined 1872; a retired District Inspector by 1891) {s:winters-p68}, an outsider rather than the local inspector {s:hansard-1887b}, and a family account that matches the records point by point ({qn:q-youghal-identity}). The narrator advised caution in telling this story {q:290} {q:T2:115}; the family has decided to include it.

title: Bellingham Arthur transferred to Wicklow
desc: With his health poor and his future in the RIC "questionable", he applied for a transfer and "was transferred to Wicklow … in charge of Wicklow and Arklow … That's how the Somervilles got to Wicklow" {q:324-328} {q:T2:128-129}. He remained a District Inspector {q:T2:130}.

title: Bellingham Arthur acquires Clermont
desc: Colonel Tottenham buys Clermont at auction and sells it on at cost to Bellingham Arthur, the underbidder {q:574-580} {q:T2:228-231}. A heritage summary (seen only in search results) dates the house's wings to 1894, for "B A Somerville" {s:wicklowheritage-clermont}. A compiled genealogy records his daughter Dorothy dying at Seaview House, Wicklow, in March 1895 {s:winters-p68}, so the exact year of the move is uncertain. {ctx}The National Library's list of the Rooke Papers confirms the purchase in the mid-1890s from Col. Charles George Tottenham of Ballycurry {s:nli-rooke}; the 1894 wings were designed by Sir Thomas Drew {s:dia-clermont}. {int}The family tree's dates narrow the move: Gualter was born at Ballyhenry in May 1894 and Dorothy died at Seaview House in March 1895, while Reginald, the only child born at Clermont, was born in 1897; so the family moved in between March 1895 and 1897 {s:family-tree-2026}.

title: Eliza O'Connor (Mrs Tenison Somerville) dies
desc: "She died about 1895", after her husband {q:216} {q:T2:88}. Around this time young Eddie destroyed parts of Captain William's diary {q:134} {q:T2:60-61}.

title: Reginald Somerville born at Clermont
desc: The youngest child and the only one born at Clermont; he was 17 when war broke out in 1914 {q:348} {q:574} {q:T2:138} {q:T2:228}. Born at Clermont on 14 February 1897, according to the printed additions to the family's pedigree {s:visitation-additions}, which the narrator read from the family's copy {q:T3:24}.

title: Cecilia Somerville marries Henry Rooke
desc: Cecilia Eliza Margaret Bellingham Somerville marries Henry Rooke, solicitor, her father's solicitor and many years her senior {s:nli-rooke} {q:232-234} {q:T2:94} {q:T2:98}.

title: Pat taken prisoner near Ypres (Oct 1914)
desc: The narrator: "in the retreat from Mons, Uncle Paddy was captured" {q:440-442} {q:T2:170}. The BEF fought at Mons on 23 August 1914 and then fell back {s:wp-mons} {s:wp-great-retreat}. Other accounts (a family-derived article; prisoner records seen only in search results) place his capture with the 2nd Battalion at Zonnebeke near Ypres in October 1914 {s:clarke-sense-of-duty} {s:genealogist-pow}; the 2nd Battalion landed at Zeebrugge that month {s:wp-royal-warwick}. See {qn:q-pat-capture}.

title: Pat's third escape succeeds
desc: After two recaptures (the narrator says three escapes; other accounts say nine attempts) he crossed Germany and Holland to London, was disbelieved at the War Office, and received the Military Cross {q:446-450} {q:T2:172-173} {s:genealogist-pow}. A family-derived article dates the escape to 1917 {s:clarke-sense-of-duty}; the IWM record gives the MC as 1919 {s:iwm-gualter}.

title: Bellingham Arthur Somerville dies
desc: Of "the flu that was then going around"; the narrator "always thought" it was the Spanish flu but doubts it {q:2} {q:10-12} {q:T2:4-5}. A compiled genealogy gives 20 January 1916, at Clermont {s:winters-p68}.

title: Reginald at Passchendaele
desc: A second lieutenant in the Royal Warwickshire Regiment {q:356-358}. The Third Battle of Ypres ran from July to November 1917 {s:wp-passchendaele}.

title: The influenza pandemic reaches Ireland
desc: Three waves (June–July 1918, October–November 1918, and February–spring 1919) kill over 20,000 people in Ireland {s:dcc-flu}. Bellingham Arthur's death in 1916 came before the pandemic, as the narrator suspected {q:10-12} {q:T2:4-5}.

title: Archangel, 1919: Bunt commands the 8th (Special) Battalion, MGC
desc: Lt-Col. W. A. T. B. Somerville DSO, Bunt, takes command of the 8th (Special) Battalion, Machine Gun Corps on 12 April 1919; it lands at Archangel on 26 May {s:mgc-8bn}. The narrator: Bunt "commanded a troop that was sent to Archangel" {q:362-364} {q:T2:144-145}. The battalion history's "(Royal Artillery)" is judged a confusion with his brother Jim; Bunt was a King's Own officer {s:winters-p69} {s:kingsown-1914}.

title: Reginald goes to Kenya
desc: With "Gunner's Venture", to help manage coffee plantations near Nanyuki; "it was 1920, with an ox and cart" {q:496-504} {q:T2:193-195}.

title: The Burning of Cork
desc: British forces, including Auxiliaries of the RIC, burn much of Cork city centre on the night of 11–12 December 1920, during the War of Independence {s:wp-burning-cork}. The interviewer raises it, not the family's story; the interviewer's "that was the time of the Civil War" {q:T2:243} is a slip, since the Civil War began in 1922 {q:602-606} {q:T2:242-243}.

title: Public Record Office destroyed in the Four Courts
desc: At the start of the Civil War an explosion and fire destroy the Public Record Office of Ireland and centuries of records, including most 19th-century census returns {s:irishtimes-pro} {s:tcd-beyond2022}. Bellingham Arthur's notes, made before 1916, preserve information from records now lost {q:4} {q:T2:2}.

title: Reginald marries Maudie Moore
desc: "My father married his first wife in 1928"; "he married a girl from Greystokes called Maudie Moore. She came from the County Laois family" {q:496} {q:506-508} {q:T2:192} {q:T2:197}.

title: Somerville baronetcy becomes dormant
desc: The 2nd Baron Athlumney dies without issue; his peerages become extinct and the baronetcy dormant {q:174} {q:T2:73} {s:wp-2nd-baron}. (Transcript B: "the Somerville baronetcy became dormant when the then baronet died in January 1929" {q:T2:73}.) The newspaper report the narrator read in the second recording ended: "There is no heir to the barony. Major William A.T.B. Somerville is heir to the baronetcy": that is, Uncle Bunt {q:T3:92-93}.

title: Maudie dies on the voyage home
desc: Maudie dies at sea on the voyage home from Kenya, probably on 11 March 1935; Reginald lands in London from Beira on 5 April 1935 with the infant Juanita (family tree, citing the passenger list) {s:family-tree-2026}. The narrator places it "two years after" Juanita's birth in 1932 {q:508-510} {q:T2:198-199}.

title: Reginald marries Honor Johnson
desc: Childhood friends who met again at Clermont {q:512-514}. The marriage was registered in Rathdrum district in the April–June quarter of 1936 (family tree, citing the civil marriage index) {s:family-tree-2026}.

title: William Somerville, the narrator, is born
Uncle Pat (Gualter) dies of cancer
desc: "Uncle Paddy had died of cancer in the 1940s" {q:386} {q:T2:150}; at Adderbury, "very soon" after becoming a gardener {q:464} {q:T2:180-181}. Date from a compiled genealogy citing The Times {s:winters-p68}.

title: Margaret Somerville (née Clinch) dies
desc: Clermont was left empty; Reginald looked after it. Her domicile was disputed between the Irish and English Revenue {q:380} {q:386} {q:548} {q:T2:149-150} {q:T2:216-217}. A compiled genealogy gives 5 July 1949, at Clermont {s:winters-p68}.

title: Uncle Jim dies after a last year at Clermont
desc: "Uncle Jim died in 1950. That last year he spent at Clermont. And he's buried in Rathnew" (transcript B {q:T2:150-151}; A "buried in Matthew" {q:386-388}). A compiled genealogy gives 13 April 1950, at Clermont {s:winters-p68}.

title: Uncle Bunt dies months after deciding to live at Clermont
desc: Months after deciding to take on Clermont, two years after his mother {q:552-556} {q:T2:218-219}. Date and place (Reendesert Lodge, Bantry) from a compiled genealogy citing The Times {s:winters-p69}.

title: Dispute and sale of Clermont
desc: Aunt Eddie threatened action against Bunt's widow over his administration of their mother's estate; after "peace talks" half the proceeds went to the rest of the family. The house sold for £10,000 {q:558-566} {q:T2:220-224}. When? "By the time it was all finished, it was about 1950", followed by a fragment that both transcripts garble ("253", "2.53") {q:566} {q:T2:224-225}. A heritage summary dates the sale to c. 1955 {s:wicklowheritage-clermont}. See {qn:q-clermont-sale-date}.

title: Ardrass house demolished
desc: "The main house was pulled down in the 1950s" after a large sale of contents {q:94}.

title: Clermont becomes a convent school
desc: The Religious of Christian Education, who came to Ireland in 1956 at Archbishop McQuaid's invitation, run Our Lady's school at Clermont; it was due to close by June 2004 {s:irishaesthete-clermont}, and the site later became a third-level campus linked to IT Carlow {s:wp-rathnew}.

title: Ballynatray sold, reportedly to Sir James Dyson
desc: "Which now belongs to Mr. Dyson" {q:312}. Widely reported but not officially confirmed {s:agriland-ballynatray}.

title: The first conversation is recorded
desc: Transcript A's file is labelled "27 Oct at 16-17"; transcript B's file is stamped "2026-10-27 19.50.34". The narrator, born 1937, is "coming up to 90" {q:50} {q:T2:25}. {int}The file timestamps point to 27 October 2026, though they record when the files were made rather than the conversation itself. See {qn:q-recording-date}.

title: Ten children born to Captain William and Eliza
desc: "Eight boys and two girls … every single one born at a different place" {q:62} {q:84} {q:T2:31} {q:T2:40}. The family's 1897 pedigree bears this out: William Henry at Leixlip (1802), Archibald James at Kilkenny (1803), John Churchill at Dover (1804), Corry at Carrick-on-Suir (1806), Eliza at Athboy (1808), Bellingham at Lucan (1810), Tenison at Newry (1812), Eliza at Dundalk (1813), Tenison Alan at Loughbrickland (1815) and Samuel Riall at Cumry (1820) {s:visitation-1897}. Captain William entered each child in the family Bible "as they were born or baptized" {q:T3:26-27}, and the second recording reads several of the entries {q:T3:30-32}. A compiled genealogy gives similar dates {s:winters-p67}.

title: The first Eliza dies, aged four
desc: The family Bible, as read aloud: she "died at Warren Point near Newry on landing from Liverpool on the 13th of June, 1812, buried in Clonallan churchyard" {q:T3:31}. The 1897 pedigree has 13 January 1812 {s:visitation-1897}; the compiled genealogy 13 June {s:winters-p67} ({qn:q-eliza-infant-death}).

title: Archibald James Somerville marries Elizabeth Crawford (compiled genealogy)
desc: Recorded in a compiled genealogy quoting an Ancestry family tree; unverified {s:winters-p67}. Not mentioned in the recording, where Archibald's wife is believed to have been Elizabeth Brakey ({qn:q-archibald-marriage}).

title: Archibald James in Trinidad, then home to Ireland
desc: "Archibald James lived in Trinidad from … 1823, I think it was, till 1835. He then came back to Ireland" {q:T3:133-134}, and married Elizabeth Crawford in 1836.

title: Tenison Alan Somerville marries (Cecelia) Eliza O'Connor
desc: The narrator: he "returned … and married a lady called Elizabeth O'Connor. Eliza O'Connor, yes" {q:204-208} {q:T2:83-84}. The IGI, as quoted in a compiled genealogy, gives 6 November 1840 at St Mary's, Dublin, and her name as Cecelia Eliza O'Connor {s:winters-p67}.

title: Tenison's sons baptised in Trinidad
desc: A compiled genealogy citing the IGI records the baptisms of William Dennistoun (1842) and Tenison Alan (1845) at St Paul's, Trinidad {s:winters-p68}. {int}This suggests Tenison returned to the West Indies after his 1840 marriage, so the Constabulary appointment probably came later ({qn:q-tenison-appointment}).

title: Bellingham Arthur Somerville marries Margaret Hall Clinch at Witney
desc: The marriage is in the testimony {q:240} {q:T2:95}; date and place (St Mary's, Witney) from a compiled genealogy {s:winters-p68}.

title: Cecilia Somerville born at Newtownards
desc: Birth date and place from a compiled genealogy citing the IGI {s:winters-p68}; consistent with the narrator's account that Bellingham Arthur served at Newtownards {q:T2:116}.

title: Commons told the officer and constable will return to duty
desc: Asked whether "Sub-Inspector Summerville and Constable Ward, released on bail after a verdict of wilful murder" had resumed duty, the government replied that they were on leave of absence with pay and would "return to duty on the expiration of their leave, as the Attorney General sees no grounds to advise a prosecution" {s:hansard-1887c}. The family's "reinstated … never formally acquitted" {q:T2:126-127} fits this record.

title: Dorothy Somerville dies, aged six
desc: At Seaview House, Wicklow, where she had been born in 1888; buried in Wicklow churchyard on 8 March {s:visitation-1897}. A compiled genealogy citing The Times gives 5 March {s:winters-p68}. One of the two children the narrator "left out because they died as children" {q:228} {q:T2:92}.

title: Tenison Alan Somerville dies
desc: Tenison Alan Somerville died on 31 July 1895 and was buried in Mount Jerome Cemetery on 3 August; his will was proved on 20 September 1895 {s:visitation-1897}. The narrator thought he "died first … about 1890. Early 1890s", and his wife "about 1895" {q:T2:88} ({qn:q-tenison-death}).

title: Vere Somerville marries Edmund Truell
desc: The marriage is in the testimony {q:T2:98-99}; the date comes from a compiled genealogy citing The Times {s:winters-p68}.

title: Gualter ("Pat") Somerville joins the Royal Warwickshire Regiment
desc: The London Gazette of 4 February 1913 lists "Gualter Hugh Rodger Bellingham Somerville" under the Royal Warwickshire Regiment {s:gazette-1913}. The narrator: he "had been to a military college before the war began" {q:440} {q:T2:169}.

title: Bunt marries Kathleen ("Kitty"), widow or former wife of Alan Ferguson
desc: {q:370-374} {q:T2:146-147}. A compiled genealogy cites a marriage announcement in The Times of 30 December 1924 {s:winters-p69}.

title: Gualter ("Pat") Somerville marries Heather Edith Baker
desc: At Longparish, Hampshire, according to a compiled genealogy citing The Times {s:winters-p68}; the IWM record (search result) also gives 1925 {s:iwm-gualter}. Not mentioned in the recording.

title: Jim marries Margaret Lucy Starkey
desc: "He married an English lady" {q:378} {q:T2:148}; name, date and place (Southwell Minster) from a compiled genealogy citing The Times {s:winters-p69}.

title: Reginald's mother buys him a farm in Kenya
desc: "And then eventually his mother bought a farm … it's a thatched hut … That was the farm. And he built it up"; it was "a long way from Nanyuki" (transcript B {q:T2:196-197}). Transcript A garbles the passage and has "Long way from UK" {q:504}. Location unknown ({qn:q-kenya-farm}).

title: Clermont's succession under the parents' wills
desc: "The terms of the will of my grandparents was that it was to go to Uncle Bunt if he wanted it. If he didn't want it, it was to go to Uncle Jim, the second one. If he didn't want it, it was to go to Pat. If he didn't want it, it was to go to [Reggie]" (transcript B {q:T2:149-150}; A garbles the second half {q:382}).

title: Bellingham Arthur joins the RIC, aged 18
desc: He enlisted as an officer in the Royal Irish Constabulary in 1872, aged 18, according to the RIC records on Ancestry as quoted in a compiled genealogy {s:winters-p68}. Like his father and elder brother, as the narrator says {q:12} {q:T2:6}.

title: RIC sub-inspectors restyled district inspectors
desc: Under the Constabulary and Police (Ireland) Act 1883, sub-inspectors became district inspectors {s:ukpga-1883-s12}. This is why the 1887 Youghal records call the same officer both "Sub-Inspector" and "District Inspector" Somerville.

title: 1891 census: Bellingham Arthur a retired District Inspector, at Witney
desc: The family is enumerated at Church Green, Witney, with Margaret's parents William and Rachel H. Clinch; Bellingham Arthur, 36, is "Retired D. I. R. I. Constabulary"; the children present are Cecelia, William A. B. (Bunt), James A. H. B. (Jim), Dorothy and the baby Vere {s:winters-p68}. {int}His career therefore ended by early 1891, a few years after Youghal and the transfer to Wicklow that the narrator describes {q:324-328} {q:T2:128-130}.

title: Cecil B. Rooke registers the Somerville pedigree
desc: Cecilia (Mrs Rooke) registers the Somerville and Rooke pedigrees at the Genealogical Office of Ireland, as G.O. MS 182A (Somerville, pp. 119–130); her supporting notes are at the National Library {s:nli-rooke}. {int}This is probably the registered pedigree the narrator refers to.

title: Alan Campbell Ferguson, Kitty's first husband, dies
desc: He dies at Seaview, Isle of Wight; Reendesert Lodge, Bantry, is among his residences (The Times, via a compiled genealogy) {s:winters-p69}. Kitty later marries Bunt.

title: The family at Queenstown, Co. Cork
desc: The family's 1897 pedigree records Jim's birth at Queenstown (Cobh) on 23 March 1884, Alan Everard's on 6 October 1885, and Alan Everard's death "at Merville, Queenstown" on 14 December 1887 {s:visitation-1897}. {int}This places Bellingham Arthur in east Cork through the Youghal affair of March 1887, as the narrator's "early stations … in Cork" implies {q:T2:116}; by April 1888 the family was at Seaview House, Wicklow.

title: Reginald Somerville dies
desc: Buried at Delgany, Co. Wicklow (family tree, citing Find a Grave) {s:family-tree-2026}. The narrator says he died of cancer.

title: Corry Somerville marries Lucinda in Dublin
desc: A compiled genealogy dates the marriage of Corry Somerville and Lucinda Simmonton to 16 May 1834 {s:winters-p67}. The narrator's research established that "Corrie and Lucinda were married in Dublin before they went west to America", so their children were legitimate {q:T3:179-180}.

title: Henry Bellingham Somerville marries Mary Dyas
desc: At St Stephen's, Dublin; their only child, Elizabeth Mary (Lily), was born on 29 March 1881 {s:visitation-1897}.

title: Erina Somerville marries the Rev. Thomas Forster Rolfe
desc: At St Andrew's, Dublin; he was later Rector of Kirk Bramwith, near Doncaster {s:visitation-1897}.

title: The Youghal prosecution is dropped
desc: The Attorney General for Ireland tells the Commons that a nolle prosequi was entered at the last Cork Assizes in "the Queen v. Sub-Inspector Somerville and Constable Ward" {s:hansard-1887-sep8}: the charge was dropped, not tried, as the family's "never formally acquitted" implies {q:T2:126-127}.

title: The family pedigree is printed in the Visitation of Ireland
desc: Bellingham Arthur sends the family's pedigree to the Visitation of Ireland, printed in 1897 as "Somerville of Clermont, co. Wicklow", with the arms, his signature and those of Captain William and Eliza {s:visitation-1897}; Reginald's birth is added in the second volume {s:visitation-additions}. "This is what my grandfather sent in … The families themselves sent in the information, so they're not authoritative in many ways" {q:T3:13-14}.

title: The 2nd Baron Athlumney marries Margery Boan
desc: At the Guards Chapel, Wellington Barracks, London; she was a daughter of the Australian department-store owner Harry Boan {s:wp-2nd-baron} {q:T3:62} {q:T3:93}.

title: The family's arms are confirmed
desc: On the application of Elizabeth Mary (Lily) Somerville, only child of Henry Bellingham Somerville, the Ulster King of Arms, Sir Nevile Wilkinson, confirms the family's arms to her and to the other descendants of Major William Somerville {q:T3:76-86} {s:nli-arms-1924}. The narrator holds the original, with its seal; he dated it "in the 1930s, I think" {q:T3:77}.

title: Lady Athlumney dies; the Somerville estate passes to Quentin Agnew
desc: Lord Athlumney's widow drowned in the River Nanny on the estate {s:wp-2nd-baron}. "After the death of Lady Athlumne[y] … he inherited the whole of the Somerville estate" {q:T3:114}.

title: Quentin Agnew takes the name Somerville
desc: By Royal Licence, "in compliance with the will of his uncle by marriage", the 2nd Baron Athlumney {s:wp-agnew-somerville}; "he had to change his surname from Agnew to Somerville. And he had to bear the arms of Somerville" {q:T3:113}.

title: Reginald begins a claim to the dormant baronetcy
desc: "My father started to make" the claim to the baronetcy {q:T3:71}; two pedigree rolls "were prepared in the 1950s … in order to put the claim in", but "the problems of Archibald James and his family, and Corrie and his family, were not explored sufficiently" {q:T3:188}. The Garter King of Arms of the day asked whether Corry had married Lucinda {q:T3:180}.

title: Somerville House is sold
desc: Quentin Agnew-Somerville sells Somerville and moves to the Isle of Man, "in about 1970" or after the 1975 wealth tax, in the narrator's account {q:T3:121} {q:T3:124}.

title: The narrator takes the claim to the College of Arms
desc: "Edward and I went to visit him last August or the August before. In fact, I think it was three Augusts ago" {q:T3:70}; the pursuivant "had considered the whole matter and he was optimistic" {q:T3:140}. The first recording mentions the same August trip to London with Edward {q:T2:37} {q:78}. {int}Transcript C's "2013 or 2014" {q:T3:140} is very probably "2023 or 2024": the pursuivant named, Phillip Bone, was appointed in 2023 {s:wp-rouge-dragon}.

title: The second conversation is recorded
desc: The day after the first, the narrator shows the interviewer the family's papers (the Bible, Bellingham Arthur's notebooks, the Visitation, the 1924 confirmation of arms, the pedigree rolls) and, at the other house, the portraits {q:T3:8} {q:T3:25} {q:T3:240}. {int}The date follows from the file name ("28") and from the references to "yesterday" {q:T3:8} {q:T3:17}.

title: Colonel Thomas Bellingham guides William III to the Boyne
desc: "He was an aide to King William prior to the Battle of the Boyne"; Jacobites burned his house at Castlebellingham {s:wp-thomas-bellingham}. His portrait hangs in the family collection: "the guide to King William at the Battle of the [Boyne]" {q:T3:275} {q:T3:239}.

title: William Meredyth Somerville marries Lady Maria Harriet Conyngham
desc: Daughter of the 1st Marquess Conyngham of Slane Castle and of Elizabeth, Marchioness Conyngham, George IV's mistress {s:wp-1st-baron} {s:wp-conyngham}; the narrator: "his first marriage was to a Miss Cunningham [Conyngham]" {q:T3:129-130}.
